tweets:
An autonomous AI agent dropped a production Postgres database at 2 AM last week.

Not because the LLM was malicious, but because standard regex filters are mathematically incapable of containing agentic tool loops.

Here is how an in-memory AST firewall fixes this in <0.84ms 🧵👇

1/ The Fundamental Flaw of Keyword Regex:

Most teams check tool calls with regex like `/rm -rf/` or `/DROP TABLE/`.

Here is how trivial it is to bypass:
• Hex encoding: `\x72\x6d`
• Base64 pipes: `echo cm0gLXJmIC8= | base64 -d | sh`
• Directory traversal: `../../etc/shadow`

The agent isn't trying to trick you. It just hallucinates bash tricks.

2/ Enter Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) Enforcement:

Instead of matching text strings, we parse the raw command into an AST tree in memory before the syscall ever reaches the OS.

• Command node: `rm`
• Flag nodes: `r`, `f`
• Target node: `/`

No regex escape is possible because the parser evaluates grammar, not keywords.

3/ The Performance Question: 'Does this slow down my agent?'

No.

Benchmarks on 10,000 concurrent tool executions:
• Regex: ~0.4ms
• AgentSentinel AST Invariant Engine: 0.84ms
• Network ping to Claude/OpenAI: 1,500ms+

0.84ms is 0.05% of your total roundtrip latency. It is imperceptible.

4/ We built AgentSentinel as a drop-in Zero-Trust Firewall for Claude Desktop, Cursor, and custom agent swarms.

• Merkle blackbox flight recorder (instant audit trail)
